title: Load and unload three boxes in Ladder
summary: Count boxes to run a fixed batch: load three, unload three, then light Done.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Count items with a counter that has a preset value.
Use one counter to stop loading and another to know the batch is finished.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/CountedQueue.ld.json the inputs Start, EyeIn and EyeOut, the outputs Run, Emit and Done, and local variables including two counters are declared, and there are no rungs yet. A press of Start must start a batch of three boxes: load them onto the belt one after another without collisions, carry them along the belt, then light Done and stop the belt as soon as the third box reaches EyeOut.
stages.checkpoint: You can say why the station needs one count at the entrance and another at the exit, and when the belt must stop.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: The scenario presses Start at {{t:200}} ms and releases it at {{t:400}} ms. Before running, follow the batch: three boxes are loaded one after another, and then the belt carries them toward EyeOut.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:CountedQueue.Run=false@100|Run OFF}} and {{v:CountedQueue.Done=false@100|Done OFF}} at {{t:100}} ms; boxes enter until three have passed EyeIn; at the end, at {{t:20000}} ms, {{v:CountedQueue.Done=true@20000|Done is ON}} and {{v:CountedQueue.Run=false@20000|Run is OFF}}.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Draw the rungs, save the program, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program has no rungs, so no box is loaded and the belt never moves. A press of Start must start the batch, release three boxes one by one without collisions, carry them toward the far end, and light Done and stop the belt as soon as the third box reaches EyeOut.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the machine move, press {{ui:toolbar.run.label}} (F5) and open the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named counted-queue and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the boxes enter one by one and travel along the belt in the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}; compare EyeIn, EyeOut, Run and Done in the trace.
stages.checkpoint: Two boxes reach the remover and the third stops in front of EyeOut; none is dropped or collides, and Done is on when the belt stops.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The scenario checks that a box reached the remover, that nothing was dropped or collided, and that Done is on and Run is off at {{t:20000}} ms. Why does the station need a second counter at EyeOut instead of stopping the belt when the EyeIn count reaches 3?
stages.checkpoint: When the third box passes EyeIn it is still near the start of the belt; only the EyeOut count tells you that all three boxes have reached EyeOut.

hints.text: Ask what the station must remember, what it must count and where, and which of those each output reads. When is it safe to release the next box?

Set Active with Start. Place two CTU blocks with R set to FALSE and PV set to 3: Loaded fed by EyeIn with Q bound to LoadedQ, and Unloaded fed by EyeOut with Q bound to UnloadedQ. Drive Emit from Start in parallel with a falling-edge contact on EyeIn, in series with Active and a normally closed LoadedQ. Drive Done from UnloadedQ, and Run from Active in series with a normally closed UnloadedQ.

faultCases: The starting program has no rungs, so no box is loaded and the belt never moves.
